commentary_segments.text: We will not discuss the effects of linear distortion in this Chapter but of nonlinear distortion. Linear distortion is a result of filter action. A perfectly linear system which shows some kind of filtering action, will distort the picture of the signal versus time. For example, a highpass filter will emphasize the steep edges of a square waveform, as they represent the higher frequencies. The output waveform has therefore peaked. It is different from the input waveform, and is distorted. This is linear distortion. It occurs for all filters.
